reading.body:
CoreSite CH1 occupies 180,000 square feet of technical space in a downtown Chicago address on South LaSalle Street. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this campus, so no power-to-rack translation is possible without inventing a number. What the square footage does establish is that this is a substantial floor-plate for a facility inside a dense urban core, where physical expansion is constrained by the building envelope rather than land.

The certifications qualify CH1 to host regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to audited controls over financial reporting and operational security respectively. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for organizations that require a formal information-security management framework, including many federal contractors. Together they mark CH1 as a compliance-oriented facility, not a raw-power facility.

Illinois has 44 mapped data centers, of which only 6 have published megawatt figures, totaling 236 MW across those six. CH1 does not appear among them, ranking seventh by published MW only in the sense that it has no published MW and therefore sits outside the ranked set. The absence of a power figure is itself informative: for a reader evaluating AI training or large-scale inference capacity, CH1 cannot be assessed on power density with the data available, and the compliance credential stack suggests its primary market is latency-sensitive or regulated enterprise workloads rather than frontier model compute.
